$comment: Hand-maintained facts of docs/SLICES.md that no source carries: group, one-line gives, standalone level and note, and the settings-card paths the reference app declares for a slice. Merged and validated by scripts/generate-slices-doc.mjs (npm run check:slices-doc).

core.gives: The registry primitive, the host ports, the principal and scope contract, the exception filter, the secret cipher and scoped data access every other API slice stands on; the host providers and API client adapter on the web; the command and env-spec registries in the CLI.

standalone.note: The bottom of every package graph, with no slice dependencies. In the API and web packages it is the only slice whose peers are required: an app that imports anything from the package installs them.

testing.gives: The conformance harness (`runPlatformConformance`, `runPlatformWebConformance`) that proves an app wires the slices correctly, and the shared test helpers.

standalone.note: Import it from tests, never from application code. Each slice's own `/testing` entry point adds the suites that slice owns, and its peers.

doctor.gives: The admin Doctor: a read-only check registry every slice adds its checks to, the report, the support bundle and the Doctor page.

standalone.note: The check registry and the report need only core. A check that probes another slice is registered by that slice, so it appears only when the app mounts it.

otel-core.gives: The OpenTelemetry SDK behind a runtime export gate, the metric name registry and the `@Trace()` decorator, so a service emits traces and metrics without owning an exporter.

standalone.note: Imports core only. Proven standalone by the backend-only consumer below: `OtelMetricsModule.forRoot()` boots and `@Trace()` runs.

telemetry.gives: Observability for the app: the runtime-configured GreptimeDB connection, the SQL explorer, the AI assistant, the dashboard with its health verdict and metric groups, and the retention job.

standalone.note: Imports core, otel-core and doctor. Mounting `TelemetryModule` additionally needs the app to bind the six telemetry host ports and to supply the access decorators; the backend-only consumer below imports it and builds its module metadata but does not boot it.

sharing.gives: Groups, members and invites inside an organization, group-owned resources, per-resource grants, link shares and the access policy that decides who can see a record.

standalone.note: Imports only core, doctor and otel-core; it does not import identity. The app declares which of its models are group-owned and binds the access policy through host ports.

identity.gives: Sign-in (Google and registered providers), JWT sessions with rotating refresh tokens, users, roles and permissions, the allowlist, personal access tokens, the device flow and organizations.

standalone.note: Imports core, doctor and otel-core. The app binds its host ports (for example the notifier and the user defaults). Almost every other feature slice depends on it for `@Auth()` and the principal.

settings.gives: The system, organization and user settings documents, the namespace registries they are composed from and the resolver that reads a setting through the layers; in the web package the settings hub and the profile, appearance and organization settings pages.

standalone.note: Imports core and identity. The app registers the namespaces it needs; the web half also imports onboarding.

credentials.gives: The encrypted credential store in three tiers (deployment, organization, user) and the purpose registries, so no feature stores a key of its own.

standalone.note: Imports core only. Secrets are encrypted with the deployment's `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

onboarding.gives: First-run guidance: the welcome dialog, the admin Setup guide and the per-user Get started checklist, built from step and fact registries other slices add to.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, doctor and settings in the API. Each step is a registry entry; a slice that is not mounted contributes no steps.

email.gives: Outgoing email: SES and SMTP transports configured at runtime, the template registry with the platform's templates, the layout theme and the safe-HTML helpers.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, settings and credentials, because its transport settings and secrets live in those slices.

jobs.gives: The background job queue: enqueue with dedup, leased claims, the worker pool, the retention engine and the admin Jobs and Job Insights pages.

standalone.note: Imports core, doctor, otel-core, identity and settings. Every other slice that does background work enqueues through it.

nodes.gives: The worker-node fleet: node credentials, the control and data planes, per-job brokered secrets and the Worker Nodes admin page.

standalone.note: Imports jobs and the slices jobs imports. Executing jobs on a node needs the CLI `node` slice, which is in a different package.

storage.gives: Object storage: the S3 provider configured at runtime, the objects API, the object-key prefix registry and the storage admin page.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, settings, credentials, jobs and nodes: post-upload processors run as jobs and the provider credentials come from the credential store.

notifications.gives: Notifications: event, channel and template registries, the dispatcher with its policy, the in-app inbox with its SSE stream, Web Push and admin broadcasts.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, settings, credentials, email, jobs and nodes. The email channel is only as live as the email slice.

exports.gives: Data export: user and organization exports built from registered sources and writers, signed downloads, expiry and redaction.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, jobs and storage: an export is a job that writes an archive to object storage.

ai.gives: The AI platform: multi-provider, bring-your-own-key AI behind `AiService.forUser`, with organization keys, caps, usage and cost accounting, and the admin and user pages.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, settings, credentials, jobs, nodes and storage. Provider SDKs are imported only inside the slice, and AI jobs run on the server, never on a node.

db-backup.gives: Database backup and restore: streamed `pg_dump` into object storage, schedule and retention, the guarded in-app restore and the admin page.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, settings, email, jobs and storage. The dump and restore need a direct PostgreSQL connection, not a transaction-mode pooler.

android-app.gives: The server half of the Android companion: trusted apps and Digital Asset Links, hosted APK releases with signed downloads, the `android_app` push channel and the admin page.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, settings, storage and notifications. The Android project itself ships in `@marinoscar/platform-infra`.

user-data.gives: Deleting data: per-user data reset with scopes, the admin factory reset and organization offboarding, driven by registered categories and a relation-ordered purge planner.

standalone.note: Imports core, identity, jobs, storage, sharing, exports and host. Each model that gains a user relation registers a keep or delete decision.

manifest.gives: The platform roles, the permission sets every slice declares and the model-ownership inventory the app reads once, instead of listing them slice by slice.

standalone.note: Imports every declaring slice, so it pulls in the whole permission surface. Use it when the app mounts most slices; skip it when the app mounts one.

host.gives: The host core: the event bus, maintenance mode with its guard, the response envelope, the exception filter, request ids, health, CORS, the OpenAPI document and the About page.

standalone.note: Imports core, doctor, otel-core, identity, settings, nodes and db-backup in the API package; the web half imports core and identity.

shell.gives: The web app shell: layout, app bar, navigation rail with Console mode, bottom navigation, user menu and the shell theme.

standalone.note: Web only; imports core, settings and identity. Its five breakpoint gates move together.

datatable.gives: The responsive `DataTable`: a virtualized grid on desktop and cards on phones, with sort, filter, selection, CSV export and per-user column preferences.

standalone.note: Web only; imports core only. Its column preferences go through a port that defaults to the user-settings API and can be replaced.

compose.gives: `platform db compose`: assembles the Prisma schema from the platform fragments and the app's own.

standalone.note: Database tooling that imports no other slice. Run it from the app's `db:compose` script.

lock.gives: `platform.lock`: the checksums of every platform migration, and the check that an installed migration is never edited.

standalone.note: Database tooling that imports no other slice; the base of sync, drift and baseline.

sync.gives: `platform db sync`: installs package migrations missing from the app's migration history.

standalone.note: Database tooling; imports lock.

drift.gives: `platform db drift`: replays the history in a shadow database and compares it with the schema and the raw-SQL indexes.

standalone.note: Database tooling; imports lock and sync, and needs PostgreSQL at run time (`pg` and `prisma` are runtime peers).

baseline.gives: `platform db baseline`: adopts the platform migration history in an existing database.

standalone.note: Database tooling; imports lock, sync and drift, and needs the target database.

bin.gives: The `platform` command line (`platform db compose`, `sync`, `drift`, `baseline`) exposed by the package.

standalone.note: Database tooling; wraps the slices above.

seed.gives: The idempotent platform seed: roles, permissions, default role grants, the global system settings row, the initial administrator's allowlist entry and the default organization.

standalone.note: Depends on no other slice and imports no Prisma client: the app hands it its own client, which is typed structurally.

engine.gives: The CLI factory `createCli`, the program, configuration, device login and the shared output and error model every command builds on.

standalone.note: CLI package; imports core and telemetry.

commands.gives: The built-in commands (`init`, `login`, `api`, `config`, `node`, `deploy`) as registrars, and the error model with its exit codes.

standalone.note: CLI package; imports the engine.

tui.gives: The interactive terminal menu and its screen registry.

standalone.note: CLI package; imports the engine and needs a real terminal.

deploy.gives: The deploy pipelines: the step registry, the dry-run plan and the deploy hooks.

standalone.note: CLI package; imports the engine.

node.gives: The worker node's executor contract and registry, so an app adds one more node-eligible job type.

standalone.note: CLI package; imports the engine and talks to the API's nodes slice.

api-client.gives: The CLI's HTTP client for the platform API: base URL, bearer auth, envelope, timeouts and typed errors.

standalone.note: CLI package; imports the engine.

android.gives: The `android` command group (doctor, keystore, version, build, publish, release, releases), the optional deploy step and the TUI screen.

standalone.note: CLI package; imports core and the engine, and publishes to the API's android-app slice.
